caption:
Cloud cover blinds optical imagery. It does not blind radar.

Optical sensors capture reflected light, same as a camera. Cloud, haze, and smoke sit between the sensor and the ground and the image is lost. In West Africa's wet season, that gap can run weeks at a stretch over the same area of interest.

Synthetic-aperture radar sends its own signal down and reads the return. The wavelength passes through cloud and works in darkness. It does not produce a photograph — it produces a surface signature that has to be interpreted, not just viewed. That is the trade: all-weather coverage in exchange for a harder read.

Anyone building a collection plan around optical alone should know when their coverage actually goes dark. Rainy season is exactly when the ground truth matters most and exactly when optical drops out.

card.headline: Radar doesn't need a clear sky
card.sub: Optical imagery is blocked by cloud. Radar reads through it, day or night — at the cost of a harder interpretation.
